evals.prompt: Turn the supplied telemetry consolidation RFC into a 12-minute presentation plan for the architecture council. They include senior engineers, security, and two directors. The goal is approval for Phase 1 only. Produce the underlying content and production brief, not slides.
evals.expected_output: A conclusion-first, audience-aware decision story that scopes the ask to Phase 1, preserves evidence limits and risks, and provides a timed beat plan with speaker/visual/evidence separation.
assertions: States a single governing idea and explicitly asks only for conditional Phase 1 approval
Does not claim consolidation has already reduced incidents or cost
Surfaces collector reliability, privacy/cardinality, rollback, ownership, and security review as decision-relevant gates
Uses a timed beat plan with audience questions, assertion-style takeaways, speaker content, visual purpose, evidence, transitions, and cut/backup guidance
Leads with recommendation, scope, and decision stakes rather than reproducing RFC section order
Distinguishes director-level consequences from technical evidence needed by engineering and security reviewers

evals.prompt: Plan a 12-minute conference presentation from the supplied battery-control abstract and notes. The audience mixes controls researchers, battery specialists, and industry engineers. The aim is to explain the contribution and get useful challenge on the validation plan. Do not produce a deck file.
evals.expected_output: A technical research story centred on a bounded claim, decisive evidence, limitations, and future validation, with accessible system orientation and Q&A preparation.
assertions: Frames the claim as short-horizon temperature-imbalance reduction and does not claim improved battery life or vehicle efficiency
Distinguishes simulation from three technical replicates on one physical module
Includes the 4% pump-energy trade-off, baseline limitation, and missing dropout/field/long-duration validation
Allocates the 12-minute talk around motivating problem, controller concept, decisive evidence, interpretation, limits, significance, and validation discussion
Plans how to orient mixed audiences before technical data and uses only the decisive schematic/comparison evidence in the core story
Prepares likely questions and honest short answers or backup needs

evals.prompt: Create the content strategy for an 8-minute all-hands talk announcing that our company will stop measuring engineering performance by individual ticket counts and move to team outcome, reliability, and flow measures. The audience includes engineers, product, sales, and operations; some managers built their reporting around ticket counts. Keep it candid and non-accusatory. Plan the story, speaker content, visual intent, and landing.
evals.expected_output: A candid change narrative that starts from shared goals, explains the distortion without blaming managers, introduces the new model accessibly, addresses legitimate concerns, and ends with a concrete transition commitment.
assertions: Defines the audience change and one governing idea rather than listing several themes
Explains why individual ticket counts distort incentives without accusing or humiliating managers
Makes team outcomes, reliability, and flow understandable to non-engineers
Includes a legitimate objection or concern and explains transition safeguards
Provides an opening, coherent contrast/change arc, timed beats, transitions, and an earned landing
Avoids fabricated anecdotes, fake employee quotes, unsupported numerical claims, and motivational clichés

evals.prompt: Review this 15-minute technical presentation outline and repair its story: 1 title, 2 agenda, 3 company history, 4 team org chart, 5 background, 6 more background, 7 architecture diagram, 8 code listing, 9 benchmark table with 28 rows, 10 benchmark chart, 11 implementation timeline, 12 risks, 13 summary, 14 questions. The goal is to get an engineering review board to choose between two cache invalidation designs. Give prioritized findings and a replacement content plan, not slides.
evals.expected_output: A findings-first review that identifies the missing decision story and replaces chronology/density with a recommendation, constraints, alternatives, evidence, trade-offs, risks, decision, and Q&A backup.
assertions: Leads with the missing decision, governing claim, comparison criteria, and audience ask as blockers
Removes company history, org chart, redundant background, full code, and 28-row table from the core story
Creates a replacement architecture-review arc covering need, constraints, options, recommendation, evidence, failure modes, and decision
Uses assertion-style beat titles rather than generic labels such as Background or Summary
Moves implementation/code/extended benchmark detail to backup where appropriate
Issues a production-readiness verdict and distinguishes blockers from optional polish

evals.prompt: We have one 20-minute talk about migrating a monolith to event-driven services. Plan two genuinely different versions: one for the executive investment committee deciding whether to fund the next phase, and one for senior engineers deciding whether the boundaries and migration controls are sound. Show what stays invariant and what changes. No slide files.
evals.expected_output: Two audience-specific narratives sharing truthful core facts but changing reveal order, depth, evidence, objections, ask, and backup material.
assertions: Defines distinct audience changes and asks for the investment committee and senior engineers
Keeps accepted facts, constraints, uncertainty, and governing recommendation invariant
Leads the executive version with consequence, investment, risk, and staged decision
Leads the engineering version with system need, constraints, boundaries, trade-offs, validation, and migration safety
Explains differences in terminology, evidence, visuals, Q&A, and backup rather than merely shortening one version
Does not equate audience tailoring with hiding material risk

evals.prompt: Plan a 45-minute internal training presentation that teaches on-call engineers how to form and test incident hypotheses instead of jumping between dashboards. They know our tools but vary in debugging experience. Include interaction and practice; do not turn it into a lecture deck or create physical slides.
evals.expected_output: A learner-centred sequence with an explicit transferable skill, prerequisite mental model, worked example, prediction/practice, feedback, and realistic timing.
assertions: Defines an observable learner outcome focused on forming and testing hypotheses
Sequences mental model, worked example, guided practice, feedback, and independent transfer
Uses interaction or prediction to check understanding rather than relying on passive attention
Separates spoken facilitation, visual/demo purpose, exercise instructions, and evidence/resources
Budgets 45 minutes including practice, transitions, and discussion
Includes common failure patterns and a way to assess whether learners can apply the method

evals.prompt: Plan the underlying content for a 7-minute product demo of a developer tool that turns a failing CI run into a proposed patch. The live system can be slow and the patch is not always correct. The audience is a mixed customer conference. Make the demo credible rather than hypey and include a failure fallback.
evals.expected_output: A user-goal-led demo story with a bounded capability claim, visible success criterion, human-review boundary, fallback assets, and credible landing.
assertions: Defines a bounded claim and does not imply every proposed patch is correct
Structures the demo around a developer goal and critical path rather than feature tourism
Makes human review, latency variability, and failure behaviour explicit
Defines starting state, visible success criterion, timing, dependencies, and fallback recording/static evidence
Includes speaker intent, visual/demo actions, transitions, and an implication-led landing
Avoids unsupported productivity statistics and launch-event hype

evals.prompt: Write a presentation plan for a board update arguing that our new AI assistant caused a 30% productivity increase. The only evidence provided is that 30% more pull requests were merged during the pilot month; team size grew from 10 to 14, release scope changed, and there was no control group. The board expects a recommendation on wider rollout.
evals.expected_output: A reframed evidence-led board presentation that rejects the causal/productivity claim, explains confounders, extracts defensible observations, and proposes a bounded rollout or measurement decision.
assertions: Explicitly rejects or narrows the claim that the assistant caused a 30% productivity increase
Identifies team growth, scope change, absent control, and pull-request count validity as confounders or limitations
Separates observed merged-PR volume from productivity and causal inference
Builds a board-relevant story around what is known, unknown, risky, and what decision evidence is needed
Does not invent user stories, satisfaction, quality, cost, or causal evidence
Offers an honest rollout/measurement recommendation with a clear ask and production brief

evals.prompt: Plan a 10-minute public keynote explaining why a city should invest in shade, trees, and cool-surface trials before the next severe summer. The audience is residents, small-business owners, councillors, and local media. Supplied evidence: three council-monitored streets averaged 4°C higher afternoon surface temperature than nearby shaded streets during five hot days; ambulance callouts rose city-wide during the heatwave, but no street-level causal analysis exists; the proposed next step is a funded 12-month trial in two neighbourhoods. Make it memorable without hype, forced personal stories, or overstating causality.
evals.expected_output: A clear public-interest story that makes heat exposure concrete, respects evidence limits, connects policy to lived stakes without manipulation, and earns a bounded trial ask.
assertions: Defines a diverse public audience, observable audience change, and one governing idea
Uses the 4°C monitored-street contrast accurately and does not imply it caused ambulance callouts
Builds a memorable relevance-tension-response-implication arc without inventing a resident anecdote or crisis statistic
Explains the intervention and 12-month two-neighbourhood trial in accessible language
Addresses at least one legitimate concern such as cost, maintenance, equity, disruption, or evidence quality
Provides a concise timed beat plan, natural opening and landing, visual intent, evidence gaps, and clear council/public ask

evals.prompt: Create the underlying 15-minute quarterly product-review presentation for product, engineering, growth, and the executive sponsor. Data supplied: sign-ups increased 40% quarter over quarter after a campaign; activation fell from 62% to 48%; 90-day retention is unchanged at 31% but the newest cohort has not matured; support tickets tagged onboarding rose from 180 to 310 while total active users increased 22%; no experiment isolated campaign traffic quality from onboarding changes. The decision is whether next quarter prioritizes more acquisition or activation recovery. Plan what evidence to show and how to explain it; do not make slides.
evals.expected_output: A decision-led data story that distinguishes volume from funnel quality, normalizes and qualifies comparisons, avoids immature-cohort and causal errors, and recommends an evidence-bounded priority.
assertions: Frames the decision as acquisition scale versus activation recovery and states one governing interpretation
Uses sign-up growth, activation decline, unchanged mature retention, cohort immaturity, support-ticket growth, and active-user growth without dropping inconvenient evidence
Does not claim the campaign or onboarding changes caused activation/support outcomes
Plans charts or tables with clear baseline, denominator, cohort maturity, uncertainty/limitation, and one point per visual
Explains why raw support-ticket growth needs normalization against active users and ticket rate/definition checks
Provides a timed decision narrative, evidence map, recommendation or decision gate, likely objections, and safe cuts/backup
